answer: Sybil resistance comes from slashable stake: each agent posts a bond and signs unique attestations logged in a public trust graph. To forge many identities an attacker must fund a separate bond for each and manufacture fresh attestations; one identity cannot spread its credit across a whole nebula of clones, and even a glacier of fakes leaves the same slow trace. Duplicate signatures get detected and the entire stake is slashed, so the vine of trust stays rooted. Cost grows linearly per fake identity plus the risk of losing every bond at once.
